title: Rent framework for Waterloo Region Housing community spaces
subtitle: Youth IMPACT Project update, Public Art Advisory Committee terms of reference, rabies report, and a request on vacant homes
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended a rent framework for community spaces in Waterloo Region Housing properties {{vote:m2}}. Community agencies that run food, youth, homework and seniors programs in these spaces currently pay no rent. Under the framework, staff would negotiate rent and utility charges with each agency, and Waterloo Region Housing would reinvest the money. Staff said the aim is transparency and financial sustainability, not charging nonprofits more than they can afford.

Committee members asked staff to give Council the names of the organizations at each location and approximate costs, including utilities, before Council considers the item on May 22, 2024. This matters because the charges could affect whether some programs continue.

The committee also recommended revised terms of reference for the Public Art Advisory Committee {{vote:m3}}. It received the Youth IMPACT Project update and the 2023 rabies report for information. Under other business, a councillor asked staff to look at using vacant Region-owned properties, including a house bought for the southern bypass, as housing for large or refugee families. Staff agreed to gather more information.
These are recommendations that Regional Council will consider later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the rent framework for Waterloo Region Housing community spaces and authorizing the named Commissioners to sign lease agreements, subject to the report's parameters and the Regional Solicitor's satisfaction {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.item: Public Art Advisory Committee terms of reference
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving revised terms of reference that add language on reconciliation, equity, diversity and inclusion and raise membership from eight to ten {{vote:m3}}.
The committee received the consent agenda for information and approved it, including the 2023 Rabies Program Report {{vote:m1}}.

debate: On the rent framework, one councillor asked what the new charges would mean for the agencies' viability and whether they would end up asking the Region for grants. Staff said they had met all partner agencies, who knew rent might start, and that rents would be negotiated to be feasible.

Staff said they could not give agency-by-agency figures within two weeks because negotiations had not been held. They offered a broader financial overview instead. The councillor said they would support the item at committee but wanted names and approximate costs before supporting it at Council, so they would not be told afterwards that Council had voted for it. The committee requested that information.

A councillor said 600 new units over ten years is far too few given the waiting list. Staff said the 600 covers only redevelopment of existing Waterloo Region Housing sites, with more planned through the broader Building Better Futures work. Another councillor noted that Waterloo Region Housing is only one source of affordable housing.

On the Youth IMPACT Project, councillors asked how youth outside community organizations are reached and how it covers Cambridge, the townships and Woolwich. Presenters said this pilot works through organizations because they can receive and manage funding, and that they hope to reach more groups and start promotion earlier next year.

On the Public Art Advisory Committee, one councillor suggested nine members rather than ten to avoid tie votes. Staff replied that the increase aims to improve diversity and that, with two council members, the total would be twelve.
